samples.summary: `clearImageSelectionForMutation` clears `selectedImage` but never calls `abortImageResizeDrag()`, so an in-flight resize drag survives the very offset shift the helper exists to protect against
samples.evidence: `abortImageResizeDrag`'s own doc comment (editor.ts:2574-2578) states: "every path that clears the image selection because the offsets moved under it has to drop the drag too, or the next `mouseup` commits the drag's size onto whatever inline now sits at that coordinate." `undoFn` (2101/2110), `redoFn` (2143) and `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (3947) do call it; `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (1288-1292) — the helper wired into `TextEditor.imageSelectionClearer` (handleCut text path, `applyPastePlan`), `insertLink`, `insertTable`, `insertImage`, `applySpellSuggestion`, every table structure API and the find-bar replace — does not. The same is true of the catch-all `selectedImage = null; render();` at editor.ts:2447. A resize drag holds the mouse but leaves the hidden textarea focused, so a Cmd/Ctrl+V (or a find-bar replace) landing mid-drag mutates the text and then `handleImageResizeMouseUp` commits `{width,height}` at the stale `(blockId, offset)` — `findImageAtOffset` only re-validates that *an* image is there, not that it is the same one, so a different image can be silently resized.

samples.summary: The IME/composition mutation path bypasses every image-selection clear: `handleKeyDown` returns on `isComposing` before `imageKeyHandler` runs, and `handleCompositionStart/End`/`handleInput` never call `imageSelectionClearer`
samples.evidence: `handleKeyDown` line 852: `if (this.composition.active || e.isComposing) return;` executes *before* the `imageKeyHandler` dispatch at line 865, so the catch-all that clears `selectedImage` never sees a composition keystroke. `handleCompositionStart` (689) calls `this.deleteSelection()` and `handleCompositionEnd` (717) calls `this.docInsertText(startPosition, finalText)` — both shift offsets — and neither calls `this.imageSelectionClearer?.()` (the only two call sites are handleCut:1260 and applyPastePlan:1353). A CJK user who clicks an image and then types leaves `selectedImage` pointing at a shifted coordinate: the overlay paints around the wrong inline, and a later Delete/cut passes `deleteSelectedImageInline`'s re-validation whenever another image has slid into that offset, removing the wrong picture. Pre-existing ordering, but it is a hole in the invariant this change establishes and enumerates.
searchedFor: grep imageSelectionClearer across repo (only handleCut and applyPastePlan call it)

samples.summary: The read-only context-menu Copy the diff's comments repeatedly cite as the reason for the whole change only appears for a *text* selection — a click-selected image can never reach it
samples.evidence: `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (docs-context-menu.tsx:74) and `getActiveSelection` (editor.ts:3358) returns null unless `selection.hasSelection()` and the range is non-collapsed; a click-selected image sets `selection.setRange(null)` (`selectImageInline`, editor.ts:1256). So with only an image selected, `hasSelection` is false, `hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection` is false and the menu does not even open in read-only. Multiple new comments assert the opposite (editor.ts:1251-1252 "the issue #870 fix never runs on a read-only document — which is exactly where the context menu now offers Copy"; editor.ts:2600-2601). Additionally `selectImageAt`/`getSelectedImage` have no non-test callers anywhere in packages/frontend, so no UI selects an image other than the canvas click. The keyboard path works; the advertised menu path does not.

samples.summary: Removing the read-only early return makes image clicks call `stopImmediatePropagation()` in view-only mode, so viewers lose caret placement / drag-selection starting on an image and document-level mousedown consumers stop seeing the click
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` no longer starts with `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2605), and the image-body branch calls `e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` at 2662-2663. Stopping propagation during the container's capture phase prevents the event from ever reaching bubble-phase listeners on `container` (`TextEditor.handleMouseDown`, which is what sets `isMouseDown` for drag selection) and on `document` — e.g. `DocsContextMenu`'s outside-click closer (`document.addEventListener("mousedown", handleClick)`, docs-context-menu.tsx:126), which will now leave an open context menu on screen when a read-only user clicks an image. In editable mode this was already the behaviour; read-only newly inherits it.

finding.summary: `handleImageResizeMouseUp` still uses throwing `getBlock` with a dead `block ?` guard — the one stale-coordinate reader the delta did not harden
finding.evidence: Line 2538: `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId); const current = block ? findImageAtOffset(block, offset) : null;`. `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:187), so the `block ?` ternary can never see a falsy value and the intended guard is dead — the throw escapes the document-level `mouseup` listener. This is exactly the hazard the delta fixed in `selectImageAt`, `getSelectedImage` and `updateSelectedImage` by switching to `findBlock`; this sibling path, which holds the same kind of stale `(blockId, offset)` coordinate across an arbitrarily long drag (during which a remote peer edit, or an undo per the finding above, can remove the block), was left on `getBlock`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `handleImageResizeMouseUp` calls the throwing `doc.getBlock(blockId)`, making the `block ?` ternary dead and letting `Block not found` escape the document-level mouseup listener. The repository does not contain that code. At packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2547 the handler calls `doc.findBlock(blockId)` — the non-throwing variant returning `Block | undefined` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:193-203, no throw) — so the `block ? findImageAtOffset(block, offset) : null` at :2548 is a live guard, backed by the `if (!current) { render(); return; }` early-out at :2549-2552. Lines :2542-2546 carry a comment giving precisely the stale-coordinate rationale the reviewer says is absent. The claim that this sibling path was "left on getBlock" while selectImageAt/getSelectedImage/updateSelectedImage were hardened is likewise contradicted: all use findBlock with null guards (editor.ts:3830-3831, :3843-3844, :3857-3858). A grep of every `doc.getBlock` occurrence in editor.ts shows no hit in the image-resize handler, and `handleImageResizeMouseUp` exists only in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts has no such handler), so there is no other copy hosting the described code. No throwing call exists on this path, so the described crash cannot fire.
